articles.title: Your Attention Is the Product Being Sold
articles.titleHinglish: Aapka Dhyan Hi Wo Cheez Hai Jo Bechi Ja Rahi Hai
articles.content:
You did not lose your attention span. It was taken by design, by teams of extremely capable people whose salaries depend on you staying for one more minute.

This is worth stating plainly because most people carry it as a personal failure — I cannot focus any more, something is wrong with me. What is actually happening is that a free app is not a gift. The exchange is your time and your attention, sold onward to advertisers, and every feature you dislike is optimised for that transaction.

The main mechanisms are simple once named. Infinite scroll removes the natural stopping point where you might have decided you were done. Autoplay makes stopping an active decision instead of a default. Unpredictable rewards — sometimes a great post, usually nothing — produce the same pull as a slot machine. Notifications manufacture urgency for things that were never urgent. Streaks and counts turn optional use into an obligation.

None of this can be defeated by deciding to be more disciplined, because you are one person and this is the output of enormous investment. What works is changing the environment so willpower is needed less.

A few things that reliably help.

Turn off every notification except messages from actual humans. This one change does more than everything else combined.

Put a small amount of friction between you and the loop. Log out. Delete the app and use the browser version, which is worse on purpose. Keep the phone in another room while working — not face down on the table, where its presence alone measurably reduces concentration.

Decide before you open. Say out loud what you are going there to do, and leave when it is done. Almost all lost hours begin with an opening that had no purpose.

Give the boredom somewhere to go. Most reaching for the phone happens in the small gaps — lift, queue, ninety seconds of waiting. If you never let those gaps exist, the mind loses the ability to sit still at all. Let yourself be bored on purpose, briefly, every day.

And protect the first and last hour of the day, which shape everything between them more than any other hours.

One fair caveat. This is not an argument that these apps are worthless or that you should quit everything. They carry your friendships, your work, your news, your entertainment. The point is only that the default settings were not designed with your interests in mind, and adjusting them is not extremism — it is just declining to accept someone else's configuration of your day.
articles.contentHinglish:
Aapka dhyan kho nahi gaya. Wo jaan bujh kar liya gaya hai, un bahut kaabil teams dwara jinki salary is baat par tiki hai ki aap ek minute aur ruko.

Yeh saaf bolna zaroori hai kyunki zyadatar log ise apni kami samajh kar uthate hain — mera dhyan hi nahi lagta, mujhme kuch gadbad hai. Ho yeh raha hai ki free app tohfa nahi hoti. Sauda yeh hai ki aapka waqt aur dhyan aage advertisers ko becha jaata hai, aur jo bhi feature aapko chubhta hai wo usi sauda ke liye optimise kiya gaya hai.

Mukhya mechanism naam dete hi simple ho jaate hain. Infinite scroll wo swabhavik rukne ki jagah hata deta hai jahan aap tay karte ki bas ho gaya. Autoplay rukne ko default ki jagah ek active faisla bana deta hai. Bina pattern wale reward — kabhi zabardast post, aksar kuch nahi — wahi khinchav banate hain jo slot machine banati hai. Notifications un cheezon ke liye jaldi banate hain jo kabhi urgent thi hi nahi. Streaks aur counts marzi ke istemaal ko farz bana dete hain.

Inme se kuch bhi "main zyada disciplined ho jaunga" se nahi haarta, kyunki aap ek insaan ho aur yeh bahut bade nivesh ka nateeja hai. Jo chalta hai wo hai maahaul badalna, taaki willpower ki zaroorat hi kam pade.

Kuch cheezein jo bharose se kaam karti hain.

Insaanon ke message ke alawa har notification band kar do. Yeh ek badlav baaki sab se zyada asar karta hai.

Aap aur loop ke beech thodi rukawat rakho. Log out kar do. App delete karke browser wala version istemaal karo, jo jaan bujh kar zyada bhaddha hai. Kaam karte waqt phone doosre kamre mein rakho — mez par ulta rakhne se nahi chalega, uski maujoodgi hi concentration kam kar deti hai, yeh naapa gaya hai.

Kholne se pehle tay karo. Bol kar kaho ki aap wahan kya karne ja rahe ho, aur kaam khatam hote hi nikal jao. Lagbhag saare kho gaye ghante aise kholne se shuru hote hain jiska koi maqsad nahi tha.

Boredom ko jagah do. Phone ki taraf haath zyadatar chhote gaps mein jaata hai — lift, line, nabbe second ka intezaar. Agar aap wo gaps kabhi hone hi nahi doge, to dimaag chup baithne ki kaabiliyat hi kho deta hai. Roz thodi der, jaan bujh kar bore ho jao.

Aur din ka pehla aur aakhri ghanta bachao — wo beech ke sab ghanton ko sabse zyada aakaar dete hain.

Ek imaandaar baat. Yeh dalil nahi hai ki yeh apps bekaar hain ya aap sab chhod do. Unme aapki dostiyan, kaam, khabrein aur manoranjan hai. Baat sirf itni hai ki default settings aapke fayde ko dhyan mein rakh kar nahi banayi gayi thi, aur unhe badalna koi charampanth nahi hai — wo bas kisi aur ke banaye hue aapke din ke configuration ko mana kar dena hai.

articles.title: Deep Work in a House Full of People
articles.titleHinglish: Bhare Hue Ghar Mein Gehra Kaam
articles.content:
Most productivity advice assumes a closed door, a desk, and silence. That is not the life of a large number of Indian students and professionals, who study in a shared room, work with a television running, and are interrupted by family who genuinely do not consider studying a reason to be left alone.

So here is the version that works in a full house.

Pick times, not conditions. Waiting for quiet means waiting forever. The two reliable windows in most homes are early morning before anyone else is up, and late night after everyone sleeps. Choose one — properly, not both — and treat it as fixed. An hour of protected time daily beats four hours of contested time.

Make the boundary visible and small. Family will interrupt open-ended studying, but they will usually respect a specific, bounded request: I am doing one hour, I will come out at eight. It gives them a deadline too, and it is far more effective than asking not to be disturbed indefinitely.

Use a signal. Headphones on means do not talk to me, and once the house learns it, it saves you the same negotiation every day. Brown noise or instrumental music without words works better than silence in a noisy house, because it masks the unpredictable sounds that break concentration rather than trying to eliminate them.

Work in units, not sessions. Twenty-five minutes with a clear target is much more survivable in an interruptible environment than a three-hour block that will inevitably be broken. If you are interrupted at minute twelve, you have lost twelve minutes, not the whole afternoon.

And keep a re-entry note. This is the most underrated trick for interrupted people. Before you get up, write one line about exactly what you were doing and what comes next. Returning to work costs most people ten to fifteen minutes of re-orientation; a single line reduces it to seconds.

Also, be realistic about what counts. In a noisy house, deep conceptual work should go to the protected hour, and everything mechanical — revision, copying notes, formatting, replying to messages, practice problems — can be done in the contested hours. Sorting tasks by how much silence they need is the single biggest gain available to someone who cannot control their environment.

And if you can, leave the house sometimes. A library, an empty classroom, a friend's place, even a park bench. Not because home is impossible, but because a place your mind associates only with work is worth a great deal, and it does not have to be yours to be useful.
articles.contentHinglish:
Zyadatar productivity ki salaah maan kar chalti hai ki band darwaza hai, mez hai, aur khamoshi hai. Bahut saare Indian students aur professionals ki zindagi aisi nahi hai — wo ek hi kamre mein padhte hain, TV chalte hue kaam karte hain, aur unhe wo ghar wale tokte hain jo padhai ko akela chhodne ki wajah maante hi nahi.

Toh yeh wo version hai jo bhare ghar mein chalta hai.

Waqt chuno, haalat nahi. Khamoshi ka intezaar matlab hamesha ka intezaar. Zyadatar gharon mein do bharosemand windows hoti hain — subah jab koi utha nahi, aur raat jab sab so gaye. Ek chuno — theek se, dono nahi — aur use pakka maano. Rozana ek ghanta bachaya hua waqt chaar ghante ke ladai wale waqt se behtar hai.

Boundary dikhne wali aur chhoti rakho. Ghar wale bina ant wali padhai ko tokenge, par wo aksar specific, seemit request ki izzat karte hain: main ek ghanta kar raha hoon, aath baje bahar aaunga. Isse unhe bhi ek deadline milti hai, aur yeh "mujhe disturb mat karo" se kahin zyada asardaar hai.

Ek signal banao. Headphones lage hain matlab baat mat karo — aur jab ghar yeh seekh leta hai, roz ki wahi negotiation bach jaati hai. Shor wale ghar mein brown noise ya bina bol wala music khamoshi se behtar kaam karta hai, kyunki wo un anpredictable awaazon ko dhak deta hai jo dhyan todti hain, unhe mitaane ki koshish nahi karta.

Units mein kaam karo, sessions mein nahi. Pachees minute ek saaf target ke saath, toke jaane wale maahaul mein teen ghante ke block se kahin zyada jhelne laayak hai — jo block waise bhi toota hi milega. Agar barahve minute par toka gaya, to barah minute gaye, poori dopahar nahi.

Aur ek re-entry note rakho. Toke jaane wale logon ke liye yeh sabse kam aanka gaya trick hai. Uthne se pehle ek line likh do ki aap theek kya kar rahe the aur aage kya aata hai. Kaam par lautne mein zyadatar logon ke dus-pandrah minut phir se track pakadne mein jaate hain; ek line usse seconds mein la deti hai.

Yeh bhi asli baat hai ki kaunsa kaam kahan karna hai. Shor wale ghar mein gehra sochne wala kaam bachaye hue ghante mein jaana chahiye, aur sab mechanical kaam — revision, notes copy karna, formatting, message ka jawab, practice questions — ladai wale ghanton mein ho sakta hai. Kaam ko is hisaab se baantna ki kisme kitni khamoshi chahiye — jis insaan ka maahaul uske haath mein nahi hai, uske liye yahi sabse bada faayda hai.

Aur ho sake to kabhi kabhi ghar se nikal jao. Library, khaali classroom, dost ka ghar, park ki bench. Isliye nahi ki ghar mein namumkin hai, balki isliye ki jis jagah ko aapka dimaag sirf kaam se jodta hai uski keemat bahut hai — aur uska aapka hona zaroori nahi.

articles.title: Multitasking Is Just Switching, and Switching Is Expensive
articles.titleHinglish: Multitasking Sirf Switching Hai, Aur Switching Mehngi Hai
articles.content:
Nobody does two things at once. What actually happens is rapid switching, and each switch has a cost you do not feel but do pay.

Here is the part that surprises people: the cost is not the seconds of switching. It is that a piece of your attention stays behind on the previous task. You check a message in the middle of writing, and even after you return, part of the mind is still composing a reply. The work continues at reduced capacity for several minutes, and because you cannot feel the reduction, you conclude you are handling both fine.

This is why an evening of studying with the phone beside you can produce three hours of time and forty minutes of work.

A few practical consequences.

Batch the interruptions instead of spreading them. Messages twice an hour, at fixed points, costs far less than the same number of messages arriving randomly. The randomness is the expensive part, not the volume.

Finish small things or write them down. An unfinished trivial task — a bill to pay, a message to send — keeps taking up capacity in the background until it is either done or written somewhere you trust. Two minutes of clearing costs less than an afternoon of low-level nagging.

Do the hard thing first. Attention is not evenly available through the day; most people have two to four good hours, usually early. Spending those on email and small tasks and leaving the difficult work for a tired evening is the most common productivity mistake there is.

And stop keeping tabs open as a to-do list. Every open tab is a small unresolved item, and they add up to a low-grade sense of not being on top of things.

One thing worth saying about a habit almost everyone has. Watching a video while eating, texting while talking, listening to a lecture at double speed while replying to a friend — these do not just cost efficiency. They remove the experience. You will not remember the meal, the conversation or the lecture, because attention is what turns an event into a memory. The tradition has a phrase for the alternative: doing one thing at a time, fully. It sounds quaint, and it is the difference between a day you lived and a day that simply passed while you were busy.
articles.contentHinglish:
Koi ek saath do kaam nahi karta. Hota yeh hai ki tezi se switching hoti hai, aur har switch ki ek keemat hai jo mehsoos nahi hoti par chukani padti hai.

Jo baat logon ko chaunka deti hai wo yeh hai: keemat switch karne ke seconds nahi hain. Keemat yeh hai ki aapke dhyan ka ek hissa pichhle kaam par hi ruka reh jaata hai. Aap likhte likhte ek message dekh lete ho, aur wapas aane ke baad bhi dimaag ka ek hissa jawab bana raha hota hai. Kaam kai minute tak kam kshamta par chalta hai, aur kyunki kami mehsoos nahi hoti, aap maan lete ho ki dono theek sambhal rahe ho.

Isiliye phone bagal mein rakh kar padhai ki ek shaam teen ghante ka waqt aur chaalis minute ka kaam bana deti hai.

Kuch practical nateeje.

Interruptions ko batch karo, phailao mat. Ghante mein do baar, fix waqt par messages — utne hi messages ke random aane se bahut kam mehnga hai. Mehnga hissa randomness hai, ginti nahi.

Chhoti cheezein khatam karo ya likh lo. Ek adhoora mamooli kaam — bill bharna, ek message bhejna — background mein kshamta khaata rehta hai jab tak ya to ho na jaaye ya kisi bharosemand jagah likh na diya jaaye. Do minute ka safaya ek poori dopahar ki halki kutkut se sasta hai.

Mushkil kaam pehle karo. Dhyan poore din barabar available nahi hota; zyadatar logon ke paas do se chaar achhe ghante hote hain, aksar shuru mein. Unhe email aur chhote kaamon par kharch karke mushkil kaam ko thaki hui shaam ke liye chhod dena — yeh sabse aam productivity ki galti hai.

Aur tabs ko to-do list ki tarah khula rakhna band karo. Har khula tab ek chhota adhoora kaam hai, aur milkar wo yeh halka ehsaas banate hain ki cheezein haath mein nahi hain.

Ek aadat ke baare mein ek baat, jo lagbhag sabki hai. Khaate hue video dekhna, baat karte hue texting, dost ko reply karte hue double speed par lecture — inki keemat sirf efficiency nahi hai. Yeh anubhav ko hi mita dete hain. Aapko na khaana yaad rahega, na baat, na lecture — kyunki dhyan hi wo cheez hai jo ghatna ko yaad mein badalta hai. Parampara ke paas dusre raaste ka naam hai: ek waqt mein ek kaam, poore mann se. Purana lagta hai, aur yahi farq hai us din mein jo aapne jiya aur us din mein jo aapke vyast rehte hue bas guzar gaya.
